title: Vale Elder
dialogue: Welcome to Hearthlight Vale, traveler. The lanterns burn brighter now that you are here.
Old Millwick has gone quiet, and I fear a letter of mine never reached him.
When your legs are steady — say, level eight — come back and I will ask a favor of you.

title: General Goods
dialogue: Potions, rope, a lantern or two — everything a green adventurer forgets to pack.
Coin up front, and I will not ask where the monsters found it.

title: Warp Keeper
dialogue: Need to be somewhere yesterday? The hearth-lines run to every town that will have me.
Step onto the glow and I will fold the road beneath your feet — for a modest fee.

title: Innkeeper
dialogue: A warm bed and warmer stew — the Hearthlight Inn never turns a tired soul away.
Rest here and the road will feel kinder in the morning, I promise you that.

title: Combat Trainer
dialogue: Grip loose, weight low, eyes on the whole field — that is how you live past level one.
Bring me proof of your first honest hunt and I will teach you a thing or two.

title: Herbalist
dialogue: Cloverleaf salve, mushroom tonic, a pinch of moonpetal — I stock what the fields give up.
Fresh cuttings today. The plains have been generous since the rains.

title: Field Scout
dialogue: Keep low in the clover — the plains look calm until something with teeth disagrees.
I have been mapping the far hedgerows. Could use sharp eyes out there before long.

title: Mycologist
dialogue: The Hollow breathes, you know — spores in, spores out, all day and night.
Some caps glow, some bite back. I could use a runner to gather the harmless sort.

title: Whisperwood Ranger
dialogue: The Whisperwood remembers every footstep. Tread it with respect.
Something has been thinning the deer trails. Walk with me and we may learn what.

title: Miller
dialogue: Wheel turns, stone grinds, flour flies — same song every day and I love it still.
Mind the sacks by the door. Trip over one and the whole town hears about it.

title: Caravan Guard
dialogue: Eyes open, blade oiled. The road pays best to those who reach the end of it.
We roll for the riverside town come dawn. Long haul, but the ale is worth it.

title: Town Mayor
dialogue: Riverside welcomes you. Keep your boots dry and your temper drier.
The docks have troubles I would rather solve quietly. Perhaps you are the quiet sort.

title: Riverside Trader
dialogue: Goods off the barges, fresh as the tide — I undercut the town square and sleep fine for it.
Haggle if you like, but my prices already float lower than most.

title: Prospector
dialogue: These foothills are lousy with crystal, if you know where the seams hide.
My last dig ran into something that dug back. Might pay a brave soul to have a look.

title: Moonwell Watcher
dialogue: The Moonwell only opens to those it deems ready. Patience, wanderer.
Bring me the sigil the glade keeps hidden — near level ten, when your spirit can bear it.

title: Gate Watch
dialogue: The east gate stays open, but the plains beyond do not forgive the careless.
Keep your blade sheathed in town. Outside the wall is another matter.

title: Hearthstone Bakery
dialogue: Honey rolls, fresh from the stone. A warm loaf mends more than you’d think.
Take one for the road — the plains are hungry work.

title: Wandering Minstrel
dialogue: A coin for a song? I know the ballad of the Moonwell, if your heart is brave.
They say every hero of the vale started right here, by this fountain.

title: Vale Child
dialogue: Are you a real adventurer? Can I see your sword? Pleeease?
I’m gonna be a ranger someday, just like Elowen in the woods!

title: Keeper of the Hearth
dialogue: May the hearthlight keep you. Rest in the vale and let its calm settle your spirit.
The Moonwell and Hollow Kiln are two halves of an older promise. Restore both, and return to me.
When their lights answer one another, the Lanternspire road will open for its final keeper.

title: Emberglass Artisan
dialogue: Careful where you step. Emberglass remembers every spark that ever touched it.
The old kiln is awake again, but a warm hearth and a hungry furnace are not the same thing.
Bring me what the shelf sheds, and together we might teach that fire some manners.

title: Dawnshore Trailwarden
dialogue: You crossed the new light and kept your footing. That makes you Dawnshore company now.
The Glasswind beacon has turned seaward, and every false reflection along the coast is answering it.
Gather what the tide leaves behind, still the beacon ward, and bring its true bearing home.

title: Coast Supply
dialogue: Saltglass for fittings, sunwake kelp for cordage, and enough stew to make the crossing sensible.
Bring me sound materials from the coast and I will turn them into something the wind cannot take.

title: Tidebreak Keeper
dialogue: Every post on this road was set to teach the storm where not to stand. Lately, it has stopped listening.
The old Reliquary is awake beyond the causeway. Watch the light beneath your feet and move before it closes.
Bring its quiet heart back here. I would rather tend a beacon than inherit another weather god.

title: Dawnshore Astronomer
dialogue: The Reliquary storm hid the upper cliffs for a century. Now the old beacon is drawing a line straight through the dawn.
Sunveil grows where that light touches stone. Gather it before the sprites drink every drop of color.
Beyond the ascent stands Sunspire Observatory. Its great lens is turning without a hand to guide it.

title: Skyglass Smith
dialogue: Up here, good footing is armor. Skyglass makes both, provided you respect its temper.
Bring petals for the glare, ore for the edge, and pinions for balance. I will handle the hammering.
The observatory mechanisms shed fine parts, but none of them fall quietly.

title: Prismwing Keeper
dialogue: The highlands do not ask us to be gentle. Gentleness is the answer we choose anyway.
The Prismwings are caught in the Archive glare. Free their silk, gather Dawnsage, and I can preserve what remains.
Maelis offers a harder road. Choose one oath carefully; the heights remember commitments.

title: Horizon Warden
dialogue: Every charging beast between here and the Archive is another hour the old mechanisms keep turning.
Bring down the Sunforge herd, turn the Raptors, and I will put a direct edge in your hand.
Aurell offers the patient road. Mine is the swift one. The highlands will only honor one.

title: Last Free Indexer
dialogue: Zenith Archive catalogued every road until it began confusing a record with a command.
Complete either highland oath. I need proof that you can choose before I ask you to reopen a place that forbids choice.
The Keeper protects the final codex. Return it blank, and the morning belongs to everyone again.

title: Highland Provisioner
dialogue: Dawnsage for fractures, sunmetal for footing, and enough cordial to make an Archive expedition respectable.
I buy from both oaths. A good workshop should not pretend one honest road is the only road.

title: Choirwood Runesinger
dialogue: Zenith kept too many endings. Choirwood has the opposite trouble: one buried voice is swallowing every other song.
Learn the canopy's living refrain before you enter Crownroot. Echo Moss and Resonant Bark remember how harmony works.
Return the Concordance Seed to me, and I will teach each of your paths the technique the old choir tried to silence.

title: Resonance Artisan
dialogue: A useful instrument does not need to be loud. It needs to leave room for the next voice.
Bring shell, antler, bark, and whatever rings beneath Crownroot. I can make the materials agree.
Keep a Clearvoice Tisane close. The sanctum attacks the song before it attacks the singer.

title: Canopy Listener
dialogue: Stand still long enough and you can hear which notes belong to the wood and which one is giving orders.
The Mossbound Cantors were gardeners once. Break the hush around them, and the canopy may remember that too.

title: Runeveil Waykeeper
dialogue: Crownroot taught the old choir to listen. Runeveil teaches its tools to listen too.
Gather the marks growing wild along the walks, then choose where their strength belongs. A bound rune is a promise you may revise.
Once the garden paths are clear, Pell can open Namesong without feeding it another fixed ending.

title: Wayglass Engraver
dialogue: One mark per piece. That limit is what turns power into a choice instead of clutter.
Binding costs nothing and breaks nothing. Change your mind at the armory whenever the road asks a different question.
Bring petals, wayglass, hide, antler, and vault dust. I can teach each material where it is useful.

title: Namesong Memorialist
dialogue: Namesong was built to remember people. The Archivore learned to treat remembrance as ownership.
Bind the strengths you trust, enter the Vault, and return the stolen names without closing them into another catalogue.
The seal is proof enough. The names themselves belong to the lives still growing around them.

title: Keeper of the Waystars
dialogue: Every light in this moor once marked a road someone freely chose. The Spire is pulling them into one answer.
Settle the creatures caught between bearings and gather enough starstuff to anchor the old crossings.
When the paths hold steady, Ione can lead you to the choice the Spire was built to deny.

title: Waystar Commissary
dialogue: The moor takes your direction before it takes your life. Anchorcord tea handles the first problem.
Bring hide, shell, pollen, and glass. I can turn a wandering haul into equipment that remembers its purpose.
The finest tools do not choose a road for you. They make sure you survive the choice.

title: Keeper of the Twelve Callings
dialogue: A job is a discipline. A calling is the promise you decide to make with it.
The Manyroad Crown binds every possible self into obedience. Bring me its keystone, and your path will remain your own.
Your first calling is freely chosen. I can retune it later, but old vows ask a price before they loosen.
